newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch seen reopening 10-year benchmark bond sales.
newsitem.headline: Dutch seen reopening 10-year benchmark bond sales.

text.p: The Dutch Finance Ministry's capital markets agency is expected to reopen sales of the 5.75 percent February 2007 government bond next Monday, analysts said on Tuesday.
They said the expectation that the agency would issue more 5.75 percent February 2000 bonds had contributed to a narrowing of the spread between Dutch and German bond yields.
The agency has previously said it will announce details of a tap issue on Friday with first subscriptions on Monday.
It has a remaining borrowing requirement of 9.5 billion guilders over the balance of 1997.

Rabobank International said the amount outstanding in the 5.75 percent February 2007, the benchmark 10-year Dutch bond, could be raised from the current 7.5 billion guilders to 15.0 billion or more by reopening tap sales.
"Due to the expectation within the market of the reopening, during last week the spread versus the 10-year Bunds declined by almost five basis points," Rabobank said in its Financial Weekly report.
Dutch 10-year yields were five basis points below those of Germany at 1335 GMT.
Rabobank said it still preferred Bunds at the "long end" of the yield curve but if Dutch yields drew level with those in Germany, this could be seen as a short-term buying level.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said in a note that privatisations and extra gas revenues would cut the remaining funding requirement to 5.0 billion guilders.
It said the next issue was most likely to be a reopening of the 10-year benchmark bond, adding it saw two alternatives.
One was a new issue, but this was unlikely as the remaining financing need was too low to provide sufficient liquidity for a new issue.
The second was a reopening of the 5.75 percent September 2002 bond, but this might clash with continuing sales of 3.0 billion guilders of the 9.0 percent January 2001 state loan.
"Selling it into the market has proved difficult and a reopening of the five-year DSL (Dutch state loan) would not be supportive to the sale," ABN AMRO said.
It said a barrage of Euro-guilder bond issues had also contributed to the underperformance of Dutch bonds.
One analyst said he expected the agency to issue another 5.00 billion guilders of the 5.75 percent February 2007 bond.
